tasks.short: List parts, estimate costs and plan installation work

steps.what: Read the actual unit specification, parts lists, technical manuals and diagrams
Choose the actual required parts and capture their identifiers, quantities and applicable prices
Populate the selected parts list and calculate extended costs and estimate totals
outputs: draft parts list and cost estimate

steps.what: Plan the actual work sequence and write procedures using the applicable technical instructions
inputs: draft parts list and cost estimate

steps.what: Check the complete parts list, cost assumptions and work procedures for the actual unit
inputs: draft parts list and cost estimate

steps.what: Save the working plan in its existing system

tasks.design: Configure a working estimate in {SPREADSHEET} or the native {OTHER} parts-and-estimating system to reuse the installer's selected lines and calculate costs. The installer still chooses compatible parts, writes the actual procedures and checks the complete working plan against {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Parts chosen from technical lists were copied into an estimate and costed manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Fixed part identifiers, quantities and prices support deterministic assembly and arithmetic.
tasks.still_hard: Unit modifications, site constraints and ambiguous diagrams need experienced judgment.
tasks.human_edge: The installer knows whether the chosen parts and procedure suit the actual building.

ambition.what: Compare the cost of an alternative compatible parts set before choosing the working plan.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: selected parts fields and quantities can populate an estimate and calculate fixed totals; compatibility and work procedures remain expert decisions.

assumptions: Boundary is an actual working parts list, cost estimate and procedure plan, not a supplier order or customer quotation. Actual purchasing, quote sending or operative work authorization must be separate final-version gated actions if undertaken.

The installer reads source documents in s1 and supplies part identifier, unit variant, quantity, price, price date and cost assumptions in s2. No free clean bill of materials or inferred compatibility is assumed.
Test native catalogue export and estimating templates before custom code. Existing automatic arithmetic earns no new saving; only actual repeated manual list assembly and costing is eligible.
Same-system save is near-zero today, represented by minimum share1 fully retained and ungated. Work planning is not author approval of a save.
Shares are unmeasured activity estimates, independent of the task class or prompt time-share prior.
unknowns: Availability of compatible unit-specific part and price fields
research_questions: Can the selected part lines populate the estimate without recreating compatibility decisions?

already_counted.description: Technical reading, selection, procedure writing and complete-plan checking remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain estimate field mappings and check pricing-rule revisions.

tasks.short: Establish the nature and extent of building damage

steps.what: Read the actual work order and locate the relevant unit and reported-damage details
Confer with the customer about the nature, timing and extent of reported damage
Determine the working damage scope and identify uncertainties needing inspection
Write the actual work-order damage clarification and unresolved inspection questions
Save the work-order clarification in the same system

tasks.design: Use the native unit-linked work-order view in {OTHER}, the mobile work-order system, to locate the reported damage context. Keep the customer conversation, damage judgment and actual clarification entry with the installer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding the correct unit history could require repeated work-order searches.
tasks.enabler_now: Native unit and work-order identifiers can provide a focused history view.
tasks.still_hard: A customer's description does not establish hidden structural damage.
tasks.human_edge: The installer asks clarifying questions and recognizes what needs physical inspection.

ambition.what: No change to inspection or repair authority.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: unit-linked work-order views can shorten retrieval while customer clarification and damage assessment stay human.

assumptions: This episode genuinely reads a work order and confers with its customer; the statement's alternative routes need their own baseline if only one occurs.

The customer supplies the damage account in s2 and the installer captures the actual clarification in s4. Unit identifier and original reported damage come from the existing work order; s1 includes resolving missing links.
Test the current native work-order view first. Already available retrieval earns zero new saving; no extra report is invented for an informal conversation.
No diagnosis, quote send or repair is hidden in the clarification. Save1 is minimum integer near-zero time, retained and ungated.
These are unmeasured episode estimates. If work-order clarification is reused for parts planning, count that actual capture once.
unknowns: Whether the episode is work-order reading, customer consultation or both
research_questions: Does the native unit link avoid an actual repeated search?

already_counted.description: Context verification, conversation, damage judgment and actual clarification writing remain counted.

incremental.description: Check unit-history links and maintain the saved view.

role.altitude: Actual building assessment and procedure planning stay with the installer; less effort goes to estimate assembly and locating work-order context.
reach: Discuss catalogue field quality with the parts coordinator; learn unit-variant and price-date conventions.
role.ambitious_version: An installer who prepares traceable cost estimates and work procedures while keeping site and compatibility decisions grounded in the actual unit.
